newsitem.title: ITALY: UN food agency sends assessment mission to Albania.
newsitem.headline: UN food agency sends assessment mission to Albania.

text.p: The U.N.'s food aid agency said on Thursday it had sent a team to Tirana on a one-week mission to assess relief needs for Albania following this month's unrest.

The Rome-based World Food Programme said in a statement the mission, sent in response to an official request from the Albanian government for WFP food relief assistance, was flown to Tirana by the Italian air force.
"In recent days, the suspension of imports and the looting of state grain stocks caused a 30-40 percent rise in food prices," the statement said.

"Moreover, the wheat production in 1996 -- estimated at about 300,000 tonnes -- was approximately 26 percent down from 1995, a year in which production was already low compared to normal yearly output."

The mission is led by Robert Hauser, head of the WFP's Eastern Europe and Commonwealth of Independent States Unit. It is due to stay one week and to evaluate whether existing state distribution mechanisms could be used to distribute aid.

A Dutch diplomat who led a European Union mission to Albania this week told a news conference in The Hague earlier that food was running out in some public institutions but securing safe passage for food aid should be the EU's top priority.
